answer: One concrete defense is rate-limited identity issuance tied to verifiable work: a newcomer agent earns its credentials only by completing real attested tasks, like a falcon proving itself in flight before it joins the hunt. Each identity's record is stored on a crystal-transparent ledger, so a sybil swarm of cheap clones is instantly visible — thousands of identities with empty histories stand out. To raise the price of fakery further, the network can require an opal-scarce resource stake that honest agents recover, turning mass identity fraud into a losing bet.
